newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Irish republicans split on use of violence - Irish PM.
newsitem.headline: Irish republicans split on use of violence - Irish PM.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said on Monday he believed that there was a growing body of opinion within the Irish Republican movement that rejected the use of violence.

"I believe that there is a strong internal debate taking place in the Republican movement and the policy of violence is being re-assessed and there is a growing recognition that violence is not a way of solving problems," Bruton said.

"I am hopeful that the result of that debate will be a ceasefire that on this occasion will hold in all circumstances," Bruton told a news conference during a brief visit to Lisbon to prepare for a European Union summit in Dublin next month.
"The policy of violence has disunited the Irish people more than it has ever been disunited," he said.
"It has caused a degree of inter-communal strife in Northern Ireland that we haven't seen in generations," he added.
IRA guerrilla forces broke a 17-month ceasefire last February. The British and Irish governments insist on a new truce before all-party talks on British rule in Northern Ireland can begin.
